question: Does a learned local trail rule (NCA: every cell updated from its 3x3 neighbourhood with shared weights) beat EA-Life's hand-coded trails (per-cell deposit + decay) on foraging?
code_base: EA-Life v4 with the review fixes (review/v4-fixes); trail update moved into a replaceable method, no other change
primary_outcome: reward_per_agent_tick (mean reward per organism per tick lived)

arms.reference: hand-coded decay (x0.985 food trail, x0.96 danger trail)
arms.fixed_ca: hand-designed CA grid: persistence {current, slower} x diffusion {0, 0.1, 0.25} (8-neighbour mean), screened on validation
arms.learned_linear: learned linear 3x3 rule on the 2 visible channels (ES on train seeds)
arms.learned_nca: learned NCA: 4 channels (2 visible, 2 hidden), perception = identity, Sobel x/y, neighbour mean minus centre; tanh MLP 16 -> 8 -> 4 plus linear path (ES on train seeds)

training.method: antithetic Gaussian evolution strategies, rank-normalised fitness, Adam
training.fitness: mean primary outcome over the 4 train seeds (common random numbers)
training.checkpoint_selection: evaluate the mean parameters on the validation seeds every 6 generations; keep the best

selection: the single non-reference arm with the highest mean paired difference vs reference on the 10 validation seeds goes to test
test: reference, no_trails and the selected arm, once, on the 20 test seeds
success_rule: selected arm beats reference on test: mean paired difference > 0, exact two-sided sign-flip p < 0.05, and relative gain >= 2%
secondary: same comparison in the mixed scenario on the test seeds
sanity_checks: the trail hook with the default rule reproduces the unmodified engine bit for bit (2 seeds)
the NCA at its initial weights reproduces the reference bit for bit (2 seeds)
kill_rule: if the selected arm fails the success rule, report no evidence; no further tuning on test seeds
